title: request: need a way to prevent mobile browser scrolling when focusing an input

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
# Problem

Mobile browsers such as Safari ([and soon Chrome once v108 ships](https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/blink-dev/c/ge7xTu-VhJ0)) resize the visual viewport when the on screen keyboard (OSK) appears. As part of this behavior, the browser will scroll the page content so the focused text input is not obscured by the OSK.

There are some use cases where this default scrolling behavior interferes with the webpage. My use case is I want to provide an app-like experience and keep the header bar visible on the screen when a text input is focused. The default scroll behavior causes the header to be pushed off screen.

I put together a CodePen that reproduces the problem: https://codepen.io/liamdebeasi/pen/RwyqjwB

Attached below are two video samples of the CodePen. The first video shows the header getting pushed offscreen when the input is focused. The second video shows the expected behavior when applying a workaround to prevent the default scrolling. This workaround works in Safari but does not work in Chrome v108+.

| default scroll behavior | custom scroll behavior |
| - | - |
| <video src="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2721089/194904088-c99be9be-b3f9-465f-ba5f-6d015c6bdf03.mp4"></video> | <video src="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2721089/194904125-ccbcd560-25d2-4364-b81c-a8ad6cce967c.mp4"></video> |

# Preferred Solution

It would be great if developers had a way to disable this default scrolling behavior so they can implement their own solution.

# Alternatives

The workaround I implemented as shown in the CodePen involves quickly resizing or moving the focused input so the browser thinks it is not obscured by the OSK. This workaround is something we do for mobile Safari, but it does not work for mobile Chrome v108+: https://github.com/ionic-team/ionic-framework/blob/main/core/src/utils/input-shims/hacks/scroll-assist.ts

I can also use the `overlaysContent` API on Virtual Keyboard (see: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/virtual-keyboard/#opting-in-to-the-new-virtual-keyboard-behavior) to prevent the scrolling, but this causes the virtual viewport to not get resized, which has negative side effects in my application.
